3. Agenda grid widget — FOUND at /e/ai-engineer-summit/public/agenda (with ?day= query param for day switching). Anonymous public page, no login required.
4. Speaker gallery widget — FOUND at /e/ai-engineer-summit/public/gallery (distinct visual grid, separate route from the speakers directory). Anonymous public page, no login required.
(Bonus 5th surface noted by the app itself, not explicitly requested by script but part of its "public surfaces" set: Itinerary /public/itinerary, JSON feed /public/feed.json, iCal feed /public/ics — all also anonymous.)

No sign-up or sign-in flow was ever triggered for any of the five widgets — the entire public program (Sessions, Speakers, Agenda, Itinerary, Gallery) is served fully anonymously with zero authentication barrier. The home page's persona buttons (Jordan Alvarez/organizer, reviewers, speakers) are for the internal /app, /r, /p role-shells only and were NOT used to view any of these public widgets — confirming persona/organizer credentials were never necessary for this scenario.

Content-approval gate: confirmed working correctly. Footer/banner on every public surface state "Approved/published session set (3)... Excluded/unapproved session set: 3 private sessions withheld" — 3 of 6 total seeded sessions are gated from public view because they are unapproved, consistent with the scenario's approval-gate precondition. Since the 3 approved sessions already populated all widgets non-trivially, there was no need to sign in as organizer Jordan Alvarez to approve more content — that step was skipped as unnecessary (widgets were not empty/near-empty).

Event name substitution: the clone's seeded/demo event is "AI Engineer Summit" (Oct 12-14, 2026), not "DevFlow Conf 2027" from the sample script; tracks are Agents/Engineering/Product (not AI Engineering/Platform & Infra/Developer Experience), formats are Talk/Workshop (not the 5-format list), rooms are Main Hall/Workshop Lab/Community Room. scenarios.scenarioName: Schedule Itinerary browsing and personal-schedule building
scenarios.summary:
Tested the Itinerary / Schedule-builder widget on the Ruckus clone at /e/ai-engineer-summit/public/itinerary.

1. ANONYMOUS ACCESS: The entire itinerary widget — browsing, day tabs, search, filters, and personal-schedule starring/saving — worked fully logged out with no account or persona selection required. No login prompt ever appeared; the app is credential-free by design for public widgets (the landing page explicitly states "Credential-free demo with persona simulation, not production auth"). This satisfies the script's "try anonymously first" step; no attendee signup was needed or possible via this surface.

2. SEEDED DATA SUBSTITUTION: The seeded event is "AI Engineer Summit" (Oct 12–14, 2026), not the sample "DevFlow Conf 2027." It has 3 published sessions across Mon/Tue (Wed has none) with tracks Agents/Engineering/Product and formats Talk/Workshop — different vocabulary from the sample data's tracks/formats, but functionally equivalent, so I exercised the flow against this seeded content per instructions.

3. CHRONOLOGICAL STRUCTURE: Day tabs (All days / Mon / Tue / Wed) correctly filter the list; sessions are grouped under day headings with per-slot time markers (10:00 AM, 11:00 AM) in ascending order. Screenshotted Monday (2 sessions) and Tuesday (1 session) — confirmed the session list changed when switching days.

4. SESSION CARD ANATOMY: Each card shows Track chip, Format chip, Room chip; linked title; a date/time line (day, start–end, timezone city) plus room; a description paragraph with a "Show more/Show less" toggle (toggle worked but text was short enough that no visible truncation occurred); a speaker chip with photo, name, and "Title · Company"; a "View details" link; and an "Add to my schedule" star toggle. "View details" navigates to a dedicated session page (not an inline expansion) showing Track/Format/Room summary, full description, and a Speakers section — screenshotted both card and detail-page states.

5. SEARCH: Typed "Agents" into the search box — correctly narrowed to "1 of 3 sessions · matched 1 by title" (Advanced Agents Workshop), then cleared successfully.

6. FILTERS: Applied a Track filter ("Engineering") which correctly narrowed the visible session set; cleared back to "All tracks."

7. PERSONAL SCHEDULE (star/Add-to-schedule): Every card has an "Add to my schedule" star button. Added "Analytical Engines in Practice" and "Advanced Agents Workshop" (closest available equivalents to the fixture titles, which don't exist in this seed) — both cards turned to a filled/pressed "Remove from my schedule ★" state and the header counter incremented to "2 saved." Screenshotted both selected cards.

8. MY SCHEDULE VIEW: Clicking "My Schedule" toggled the list to show "2 of 2 in My Schedule" — exactly the two starred sessions, in correct time order (Mon 10:00 AM, Tue 10:00 AM). Screenshotted.

9. PERSISTENCE: Did a full browser navigation reload of the itinerary URL. The header still reported "2 saved" and both stars remained in "Remove from my schedule" (pressed) state; re-opening My Schedule view again showed the same 2 sessions — confirming client-side (browser-local, per the on-page copy "saved in this browser") persistence across reload. Screenshotted post-reload state.

10. EXPORT/ICS: An "Export My Schedule (.ics)" link is present, with its href dynamically including the ids of currently-saved sessions (…?ids=ses-analytical,ses-workshop). Clicked it once; the browser did not navigate away and no visible in-app confirmation/toast appeared, consistent with a direct file-download response — did not open the downloaded file per instructions. Screenshotted the control before/after click.

11. REMOVE: Clicked "Remove from my schedule" on one of the two sessions; the counter updated to "1 saved" and the My Schedule view correctly narrowed to "1 of 1 in My Schedule," showing only the remaining session. Screenshotted.

All success signals were captured: two different day screenshots, one fully-annotated session card and its detail-page expansion, two sessions in added/selected state, the personal schedule view with exactly those two, a post-reload persistence screenshot, the export/ics control interaction, and the remove-to-single-session state. Browsing and schedule-building were both anonymous throughout — no attendee account was ever required or offered by this widget.

scenarios.scenarioName: Build and organize the speaker database
scenarios.summary:
Fully exercised the Speaker CRM (cross-event) feature in Ruckus at /app/crm as organizer Jordan Alvarez (signed in via persona-card selection on landing page; app uses header/persona simulation, not real signup/login).

1. NAV: Confirmed a genuine org-level CRM distinct from the per-event 'Speakers' link — top nav has both 'Speakers' (event-scoped) and 'Speaker CRM' (/app/crm, described as "Organization-level speaker directory across events — contacts, pipeline, segments, and import"). Screenshot captured.

2. IMPORT: Used the CSV import UI at /app/crm/import. Uploaded the speakers.csv fixture (Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor, Dana Kowalski). The Validate step showed a clear pre-commit preview table with per-row status: Priya and Marcus flagged 'would_merge' (matched existing emails already seeded from the event-level import) and Dana flagged 'would_create'. Completing Import correctly deduplicated: contact count rose from 11→12 (only Dana added as new; Priya/Marcus merged, not duplicated), and activity log recorded 'Merged from CSV import' notes on both. Screenshots captured of validation table and populated directory (12 contacts, names+emails+company+stage+tags visible).

3. SEARCH: Typed 'Priya' into directory search — narrowed correctly to the 2 existing Priya Raman rows (shows two different pre-existing emails, itself evidence of a pre-existing duplicate pair). Clearing via the 'Clear filters' button revealed a UI BUG: the table state did not refresh (kept showing 2 of 12 with a self-contradictory 'no filters' label) until the page was fully reloaded/navigated, which did correctly restore all 12 rows.

4. FILTERS: Applied a company filter (Cloudreach Labs) → 1 of 12 with visible criteria text. Added a second filter (tag=agents) → 1 of 12 with both criteria shown ('filtered by tag agents · company Cloudreach Labs'). Removed company filter, kept tag=agents alone → 2 of 12 (Lin Clark, Marcus Okafor). Screenshots captured at each step.

5. SEGMENTS: Segments page (/app/crm/segments) already had a pre-seeded segment named 'AI Experts' (3 contacts) and a pre-seeded custom field definition 'Speaker Type' (dropdown: Internal/External) — noted as pre-existing seed data matching this scenario's target values. Still created a new segment via the Save-segment form using name 'AI Experts' + tag filter 'agents' (2 contacts); it appeared in the segments list distinct from the pre-seeded one. Opening 'Open in directory' navigated to /app/crm?tag=agents but the tag filter dropdown did NOT auto-apply from the URL param (a bug) — had to manually reselect the tag filter to see the 2-member list, which was then screenshotted.

6. CONTACT PROFILE: Opened Priya Raman's org-level profile (/app/crm/contacts/crm-ab5ed8fe). Profile shows notes, stage pipeline buttons, custom fields, event history, stage timeline, and a 'Possible duplicates' panel. Added internal note 'Met at DevFlow 2026 - strong on CI topics; shortlist for keynote.' — saved and persisted after full page reload (confirmed via reload+snapshot). Event history section showed 'No linked events yet' (present but empty for this contact) and stage-timeline activity feed showed real history entries (stage moves, note additions, merges) — both features exist and were screenshotted.

7. CUSTOM FIELD: Set the pre-existing 'Speaker Type' dropdown field to 'External' on Priya's profile; change auto-saved (confirmed by a toast/footer text 'Speaker Type: External') and persisted after reload — screenshotted before/after.

8. DUPLICATE + MERGE: Created a new contact 'Priya Raman' / priya.raman.alt@sbek-test.example.com via the directory's Add-contact form (13th contact). Opening its profile showed a 'Possible duplicates' panel automatically listing BOTH other Priya Raman records with 'Merge into this' actions — real duplicate detection, not just a warning banner. From the original enriched profile (crm-ab5ed8fe), clicked 'Merge into this' for the new duplicate. Merge executed immediately with no confirmation/undo-warning dialog. Result: contact count dropped from 13 back to 12, the survivor's notes/custom-field values were retained, and a new note 'Merged duplicate Priya Raman <priya.raman.alt@...>' was appended to its history. Screenshots captured of the duplicate-detection panel and the post-merge survivor state.

9. FINAL: Screenshotted the directory table in its ending state (12 contacts).

BUGS/GAPS RECORDED: (a) 'Clear filters' button leaves a stale/inconsistent table view until a full page reload; (b) segment 'Open in directory' link passes a URL query param that the directory page does not auto-apply to its filter controls; (c) merge action has no confirmation or 'cannot be undone' warning. None of these blocked the underlying capability — all core CRM-S1 features (cross-event directory, CSV import with dedup, search, multi-filter, segments, notes with persistence, custom fields, and duplicate-merge) are implemented and functional.

Executed CRM-S2 end-to-end against the Ruckus app's persona-simulation demo (no real signup — clicking "Jordan Alvarez" persona card logs in as the seeded organizer; noted as a substitution for real auth).

1. Sign-in / directory: Confirmed the CRM directory (/app/crm) already had Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor, and Dana Kowalski seeded (12 contacts total) from the CRM-S1 fixture data — no need to recreate them.

2. Event existence: DevFlow Conf 2027 already existed in the event switcher (alongside AI Engineer Summit, Forward Summit 2028, and a "DevFlow Conf 2027 Test" duplicate) — switched into it successfully.

3. Pipeline board: Found at /app/crm/pipeline, labeled "Sourcing pipeline." Screenshotted full kanban with columns Prospect(3)/Contacted(1)/Invited(1)/Confirmed(5)/Alumni(2)/Declined(0) — a renamed equivalent of the target's stage vocabulary. All directory contacts are already enrolled.

4. Enroll: Used the "Add prospect" dropdown+button to enroll Marcus Okafor into Prospect stage. Screenshotted the enroll UI and the new/updated card. NOTE: the enroll form only offers a contact picker — no score/rationale fields as the script hoped; recorded as a gap.

5. Move forward two stages: Moved Marcus Okafor Prospect→Contacted→Invited via inline "→ stage" buttons. Screenshotted board before/after, then reloaded the page and confirmed the card remained in "Invited."

6. Card detail + note: Opened Marcus Okafor's detail page, which shows Notes, a "Stage timeline" (timestamped stage-transition log), and Event history. Added note "Left voicemail 2027-01-15; follow up next week." — saved successfully with a toast and appeared in the notes list with timestamp. Reloaded the page and confirmed both the note and stage timeline persisted.

7. Reuse across events: Used the contact detail's "Add to event" control (Event=DevFlow Conf 2027, Role=Speaker). It returned a success toast ("Added to event as speaker," "Created speaker: ... DevFlow Conf 2027") and added an Event-history / Stage-timeline entry. HOWEVER, when navigating to DevFlow Conf 2027's Speakers page (/app/speakers) to verify, the page consistently failed with "Could not load the speaker roster: event not found" (reproduced after Retry and Reload). The same /app/speakers route worked fine when switched back to the seeded "AI Engineer Summit" event, confirming this is a DevFlow-Conf-2027-specific bug, not a general outage. Directly opening the created speaker record (/app/speakers/spk-crm-66a477ea) also returned "speaker not found." This is a genuine functional defect: the "reuse across events" UI exists and reports success, but the resulting speaker record could not be verified/viewed in the target event's roster.

8. Bulk outreach: Selected 2 contacts (Marcus Okafor, Priya Raman-2) via checkboxes; "Communicate (2)" button opened a composer with Subject + Body fields pre-filled with a merge-tag template ({{name}}, {{event_name}}). Filled subject "Speak at DevFlow Conf 2027?" and a body inviting them to submit, using the offered merge tags. No live "resolved" personalization preview was shown before sending. Clicked "Send now" — got per-recipient activity-log entries ("Email sent: ... (sent)") plus an aggregate campaign entry ("2 recipient(s)"). Verified in Campaign History (/app/crm/campaigns): campaign listed with subject/body, though the body is stored with raw unresolved merge tags (no confirmed per-recipient personalization resolution visible in the log — reasonable given the app's disclosed "mock mailer").

9. Dashboard: No dedicated cross-event CRM analytics dashboard (with widgets like top companies/speaker source/region) exists. The closest equivalent is the /app/crm directory's KPI tiles: Contacts=12 (consistent with "Showing 12 of 12 contacts" in the table), Segments=3, Campaigns=1 (after this session's send), a "Top tag" widget, and a "Contacts by stage" breakdown — clicking these filters the directory rather than navigating to deeper analytics. The per-event /app Command page is a separate, event-scoped operational dashboard (submissions/review/onboarding), not an org-wide CRM view. Recorded absence of company/source/region widgets explicitly.

Persistence of a logistics value is demonstrated: 'Vegetarian' entered in the portal profile survived save and a full portal reload and is shown on the organizer-side record's Dietary requirements field alongside the synced bio/headshot. The specific travel-preference sample text was never typed (the field still shows its placeholder), so persistence is evidenced through the sibling logistics field rather than the travel field itself.
Manual verification: Cloudflare cron (hourly) runs autonomously across ALL events with per-event evidence (verified live 2026-08-10: lastRunAt + 8 sends; automation tests).

defects.description: The pre-existing event named 'DevFlow Conf 2027' consistently fails to load the Speakers roster and Schedule with 'Could not load the speaker roster — event not found', across repeated Retry, reload and re-navigation, even though /app/submissions loads real data for that same event. This blocked the whole speaker-management flow for that event and forced creation of a duplicate 'DevFlow Conf 2027 Test' event.

Event context does not fully propagate on switching events: the sidebar footer keeps showing the stale label 'AI Engineer Summit · in-memory demo' after switching, and the Speakers page briefly renders another event's roster before the fetch resolves (agent initially mistook this for cross-event data leakage).

The onboarding-progress completion filter ('All speakers / Complete only / Incomplete only') filters only the progress table; the speaker card list below continues to show every speaker, so 'Complete only' shows an empty table above four visible speaker cards — misleading state.
defects.where: /app/speakers onboarding progress panel vs speaker cards

defects.description: Inconsistent completion percentages for the same speaker: the progress table shows Priya Raman at 50% while her roster card and portal dashboard show 67%.
The same uploaded headshot is listed twice on the organizer record (once as 'headshot · public' and once as 'content · submitted'), creating duplicate deliverable rows for one file.

Most logged communications display 'Logged Undeliverable' / 'Send failed' status, so speakers would not actually receive invitations or announcements; the app labels this an honest mock provider, but no successful send path was observable for the speaker addresses used.
defects.where: Comms per-recipient send log; speaker record COMMUNICATION HISTORY

defects.description: Speaker-portal access is by an unauthenticated 'Demo persona' switcher, so any visitor can view any speaker's scoped portal; per-speaker scoping is presentational rather than enforced (self-declared as persona simulation, not production auth).

areas.notes: Two of three scenarios (SPK-S1, SPK-S3) ended at the 90-turn limit, largely consumed by working around the broken 'DevFlow Conf 2027' event and by the resulting event/data mismatch (the synced Priya record lives under the seeded 'AI Engineer Summit' event). As a result several rubric actions were never exercised even though their controls are visibly present: roster search, workflow-status change + status filter, the Assign task form, the organizer bio sentinel edit, and the actual bulk-send confirmation. Those items are scored partial where surrounding evidence shows the surface and adjacent behaviour, not as feature absence. The portal half (SPK-S2) ran cleanly and the portal→organizer sync of bio, social links, dietary field and headshot file is the strongest evidenced part of this area.

scenarios.scenarioName: Organizer builds the speaker roster and assigns onboarding tasks
scenarios.summary: Turn limit (90) reached before the scenario finished.
observations: BUG: Switching current event to "DevFlow Conf 2027" via the event switcher updates the banner label but the Speakers page then fails to load with "Could not load the speaker roster / event not found". The sidebar still shows stale text "AI Engineer Summit · in-memory demo" even after switching, suggesting the event context did not fully propagate. Retry does not fix it.

CRM directory (org-level speaker directory, not event-scoped) already contains contacts resembling our fixture identities: Priya Raman (priya.speaker@sbek-test.example.com, stage=invited), Marcus Okafor (marcus.speaker@sbek-test.example.com, stage=contacted), Jordan Alvarez organizer, Sam Whitfield reviewer — all with @sbek-test.example.com addresses, distinct from the fixture's @example.com addresses. This indicates the app was pre-seeded/previously exercised with similar sentinel data. There's also a separate "Priya Raman" with sbek-speaker@example.com (stage=confirmed) already existing — meaning duplicate contact entries for the same person under different emails exist in this org directory. Will proceed using the per-event Speakers page (/app/speakers) as the primary roster surface per script step 3, since CRM is described as cross-event.

CRITICAL BUG: The event "DevFlow Conf 2027" (pre-existing, matches fixture name) fails to load on both /app/speakers and /app/schedule with "Could not load the speaker roster / event not found" — even though /app/submissions works fine for the same event and shows real submission data. Switching persists (banner shows "Current event: DevFlow Conf 2027") but the Speakers page's API call fails consistently across multiple retries, reloads, and re-navigations. This blocks performing the Speaker Management scenario against DevFlow Conf 2027 as scripted. Switching back to "AI Engineer Summit" event loads its Speakers page fine, with real data (Priya Raman, Ada Lovelace, Margaret Hamilton, Sam Rivera) including "Add speaker", "Import CSV", "Assign task" buttons, per-speaker "Send invite"/"Nudge", task completion columns, search/filter. I will proceed exercising the Speaker Management feature set against AI Engineer Summit (the working event) to gather complete evidence of the feature's functionality, since DevFlow Conf 2027's speakers module appears broken/inaccessible.

Switching to "Forward Summit 2028" shows the identical speaker roster (Priya Raman, Ada Lovelace, Margaret Hamilton, Sam Rivera with identical percentages/tasks) as "AI Engineer Summit" — suggesting the Speakers page may not be properly scoping data per-event (possible stale cache / shared demo data), though the top banner label does update correctly. Only "DevFlow Conf 2027" produced an explicit "event not found" error. This is further evidence of event-scoping issues in this app when switching events on the Speakers page.

Correction to prior observation: Forward Summit 2028 Speakers page, after full reload, correctly shows "No speakers match" / empty roster (0 complete, 0/0) — my earlier snapshot showing Priya etc. under Forward Summit 2028 was a stale render before the fetch completed, not true data leakage. So the app does correctly scope speakers per event for AI Engineer Summit and Forward Summit 2028. Only DevFlow Conf 2027 (the fixture-named event) actually errors with "event not found" — a real defect specific to that event's speaker/schedule endpoints.

Created new event "DevFlow Conf 2027 Test" (since pre-seeded "DevFlow Conf 2027" event errors with "event not found" on Speakers/Schedule pages — a real app bug) via the event-switcher's "New event" form, filling name, dates 2027-05-12 to 2027-05-14, venue Moscone West SF, rooms (Main Stage, Room 2A, Room 2B, Workshop Lab), and tracks (AI Engineering, Platform & Infra, Developer Experience) matching fixture data. Event created successfully and its Speakers page loads correctly showing empty state ("No speakers match... Accept a submission, add manually, or import CSV"), confirming multi-event creation IS supported by the app despite the broken pre-seeded DevFlow event.

Add speaker form fields available: name, email, title, company, Bio, Travel preference, plus a checkbox for "different person with same name" dedup logic. No dedicated Twitter/LinkedIn/social fields, no dietary or t-shirt size fields in this quick-add form — those fixture fields could not be entered here (may exist on the full speaker profile page).

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker completes onboarding in the portal
scenarios.summary:
Executed SPK-S2 speaker onboarding scenario against the Ruckus app's speaker portal (/p/*).

1. SIGN-IN: From the app root, the "Enter a role shell" persona picker already listed "Priya Raman · sbek-speaker@example.com" as a pre-seeded speaker card (roster link from a prior scenario). Clicked it to enter the speaker portal at /p — no separate signup flow was needed or offered; identity is via persona-header simulation, not real auth (app's own stated design: "Identity is header/persona simulation — not multi-tenant auth").

2. DASHBOARD IDENTIFICATION: /p shows "Welcome, Priya" heading, onboarding progress bar, her assigned session, and a "Latest message" panel — clearly a speaker-facing view distinct from the organizer admin shell (/app/*). Screenshot captured.

3. SCOPING CHECK: Walked every portal page (Home, Talks, Tasks, Deliverables, Resources, Profile). No trace of Marcus Okafor, Dana Kowalski, or any other speaker's name/session/task data appeared on any page. The only place other speaker names appear is a labeled "Demo persona" switcher used to view a different persona's own shell — not a leak. The Deliverables page explicitly states "Deliverables are scoped to the signed-in speaker." Recorded as an observation.

4. SESSION VISIBLE: Both the dashboard and the Talks ("My submissions") page show "Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale" with status "Scheduled" and time/room "9:00 AM–9:45 AM Los Angeles · Main Hall." Screenshots captured.

5. PROFILE EDIT: Opened /p/profile, filled Title, Company, Bio (with sentinel SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01 appended), LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Dietary from the fixture, and uploaded headshot.png via the file input. Screenshotted the filled form pre-save, saved, and confirmed the saved page rendered an "img Priya Raman headshot" element.

6. PERSISTENCE: Reloaded /p/profile — bio sentinel and headshot both persisted. Screenshotted.

7-11. TASKS: The app's seeded task set for Priya (Complete your speaker profile, Upload headshot, Upload presentation slides, Upload supporting document — all with due dates) differs from the fixture's 5-task list; there is no "Confirm participation" task and no "Sign speaker release form" task anywhere in Tasks or Deliverables — recorded explicitly as a missing/substituted capability. "Complete your speaker profile" and "Upload headshot" auto-flipped to Done as a direct side effect of the step-5 profile save (bio ≥20 chars + headshot upload), per on-page copy ("Save with 20+ characters to auto-complete this task" / "This task is complete — organizer deliverable and portal completion agree") — there was no separate Mark-Complete/checkbox control to exercise for these two types, since status is derived, not independently toggled. "Upload presentation slides" and "Upload supporting document" were left Pending, serving as the closest available substitute for "leave one task incomplete." Reloaded /p/tasks and /p (dashboard now shows Onboarding 67%, 2/3 required tasks complete) — the 2-done/2-pending state persisted after reload. Screenshots captured of before/after and final reloaded state.

All success signals were verified except where the app's own task vocabulary diverged from the fixture's; those divergences are documented as explicit findings rather than papered over.
observations: Portal dashboard at /p identifies speaker as Priya Raman ("Welcome, Priya"), shows her session "Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale" with time/room (9:00-9:45 AM Los Angeles, Main Hall), onboarding progress (0/3 required tasks), and a persona switcher dropdown (Demo persona) listing only speaker personas for demo switching - this is a demo mechanism, not a data leak, since selecting a different persona would presumably reload with that persona's own scoped data. Current event shown is "AI Engineer Summit" (seeded demo event) not "DevFlow Conf 2027" from the fixture - the app has its own seeded event/data, consistent with prior scenario building on this seed.

Tasks page /p/tasks shows 4 tasks for Priya: "Complete your speaker profile" (Done, due 2026-10-01), "Upload headshot" (Done, due 2026-10-01), "Upload presentation slides" (Pending, due 2026-10-01), "Upload supporting document" (Pending, due 2026-10-01). This differs from the fixture's tasks_for_speakers list (Confirm participation, Upload headshot, Complete bio and profile, Upload final slides by 2027-05-01, Sign speaker release form) - there is no "Confirm participation" task and no "Sign speaker release form" task in this app's seeded task set; instead it has "Upload supporting document". The "Complete your speaker profile" and "Upload headshot" tasks appear to have been auto-marked Done as a side effect of saving the profile form with bio+headshot in the previous step, rather than via an explicit standalone "mark complete" action - will verify by inspecting the task detail pages.

This app's seeded task set for Priya (4 tasks: Complete your speaker profile, Upload headshot, Upload presentation slides, Upload supporting document) differs from the fixture's 5-task list (Confirm participation, Upload headshot, Complete bio and profile, Upload final slides, Sign speaker release form). There is no "Confirm participation" task and no "Sign speaker release form" task available anywhere in the portal - checked Tasks and Deliverables pages. Completing the "Complete your speaker profile" and "Upload headshot" tasks via a standalone Mark-Complete/Confirm control was not applicable here: both tasks auto-completed as a side effect of the profile-save action in step 5 (saving bio ≥20 chars + uploading headshot flips them to Done automatically, per task page text "Save with 20+ characters to auto-complete this task" and "This task is complete — organizer deliverable and portal completion agree"). No explicit checkbox/Mark Complete button exists on these two task types; they are computed/derived status, not independently togglable. The two remaining tasks (Upload presentation slides, Upload supporting document) are left Pending/incomplete, serving as the closest available substitute for the script's "leave Sign speaker release form incomplete" instruction, since that specific task type does not exist in this app.

Confirmed scoping across all portal pages (Home, Talks, Tasks, Deliverables, Resources, Profile): no reference to Marcus Okafor, Dana Kowalski, or any other speaker's name, session, or task data appears anywhere in Priya's portal. The only place other speaker names appear is the "Demo persona" dropdown selector used for switching which persona's shell to view (a demo/dev convenience, clearly labeled), not a data leak within Priya's own scoped views. Deliverables page explicitly states "Deliverables are scoped to the signed-in speaker — use the persona selector in the header to view another speaker's portal" confirming intentional per-speaker scoping design.

observations: Found two distinct events with overlapping speaker names. "DevFlow Conf 2027" (the event created for this SBEK persona set, matching speaker2=Marcus Okafor) shows Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor, Dana Kowalski all at 0%/invited with no headshots and no bio sync data. This suggests the portal-side bio/headshot edit from the "earlier scenario" prerequisite either was not carried into this session (app state resets in-memory per Worker restart, as stated on the homepage) or the DevFlow event here is a freshly-created shell without the seeded portal sync. Proceeding to check DevFlow Conf 2027 Priya's record directly to confirm.

BUG: The event named exactly "DevFlow Conf 2027" (plain, no suffix) consistently fails to load on /app/speakers and /app/speakers/:id with "Could not load the speaker roster / event not found", even after Retry/Reload. This reproduces reliably across multiple navigation attempts. Meanwhile "DevFlow Conf 2027 Test" (a duplicate event, same venue) loads fine and shows a roster of Dana Kowalski, Marcus Okafor, Priya Raman all at 0%/invited with no headshots/bios synced — i.e., a fresh untouched roster, not one with the portal-side bio/headshot edits described in the scenario prerequisite. This suggests either: (a) the 'earlier scenario' work (Priya's portal edits with bio sentinel SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01 and headshot) was performed against a DIFFERENT event/session that no longer matches this session's live event list, or (b) the app's in-memory demo state reset per the site's own disclaimer ('Memory resets on Worker restart'), losing prior portal edits. Also note: 'AI Engineer Summit' (the default demo event) happens to have a speaker named 'Priya Raman' pre-seeded with a real headshot and profile at 67% - but this is the built-in demo speaker, not the SBEK-fixture speaker tied to sbek-speaker@example.com, and her bio does not appear to contain the portal sentinel text (to be verified).

On "DevFlow Conf 2027 Test" event, Priya Raman's organizer record shows bio = "Leads the build-tooling platform team at Latticework Systems." (does NOT contain sentinel SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01) and headshot field shows only an "Upload headshot" button (no headshot image displayed) — i.e., no portal-side sync happened for this event's Priya record. This is a fresh/seed record. Will check the "AI Engineer Summit" event's Priya Raman record next, which showed 67% completion and a visible headshot thumbnail in the roster.

FOUND: Priya Raman's synced organizer record lives under event "AI Engineer Summit" (evt-ai-summit-2026), NOT under any event literally named "DevFlow Conf 2027" — despite the event switcher offering "DevFlow Conf 2027" and "DevFlow Conf 2027 Test" as separate entries, neither of those actually contains the portal-synced Priya record. This is a naming/multi-event mismatch: the acceptance email history even says "Your talk has been accepted to DevFlow Conf 2027" (matching the sample data subject) while the event is internally still called/keyed as AI Engineer Summit (evt-ai-summit-2026). Bio field confirmed to contain sentinel: "...developer productivity metrics. SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01" — portal edit synced correctly. Headshot: file listing under Files/deliverables shows "headshot.png · headshot · 2026-08-12T21:49:27 · public" with a "View / download headshot" link, and a duplicate content entry "headshot.png content · submitted". Dietary field shows "Vegetarian" (matches sample). LinkedIn matches sample URL. Continuing evaluation using this event as the working "DevFlow Conf 2027" equivalent, since it holds the actual synced data.

Headshot download/view link works correctly - clicking "View / download headshot" opens the actual image file (256x256 PNG) at /api/events/evt-ai-summit-2026/content/files/content-82e92a47/versions/version-8ae90798 without error. Confirms file storage + retrieval works end-to-end.

Task completion filter ("All speakers" / "Complete only" / "Incomplete only") exists on the Speakers list page. Setting to "Complete only" correctly returns zero rows in the table (since no speaker in this event is 100% task-complete) while the speaker cards below still show all 4 (cards section appears unaffected by the filter - likely a separate list not tied to the same filter, a minor UI inconsistency). Setting to "Incomplete only" showed all 4 speakers (all have at least one incomplete task) matching expectation. Marcus Okafor (speaker2 in sample data) is not present in the "AI Engineer Summit" event roster (which has Priya/Ada/Margaret/Sam Rivera) - he only exists in "DevFlow Conf 2027" / "DevFlow Conf 2027 Test" events, which do not have the synced Priya data.
